prediction.likelyOutcome: Carmichael is likely to prevail on liability given strong evidence of prior similar crimes, CVS's own knowledge of the danger, guard removal, and converging expert/officer/corporate testimony on deterrence and causation; CVS's superior-knowledge defense is a poor factual fit. The main risks are a comparative-fault reduction tied to Carmichael's own use of a firearm and, if post-verdict, a real possibility of a new trial on the refused jury instruction. The quoted record supports at minimum the $725,800 in medical specials, but the true value is almost certainly substantially higher once unquantified pain-and-suffering and future-damages evidence (reflected in the baseline's much larger figures) is factored in.

outcome.description: A Fulton County jury returned a total verdict of $45,000,000, found CVS 95% at fault and the claimant 5% at fault (0% to the shooter and to the acquaintance), and awarded an adjusted $42,750,000 against CVS. The trial court denied CVS's motions for new trial and j.n.o.v. The Court of Appeals of Georgia affirmed on November 8, 2021, and the Supreme Court of Georgia, on certiorari, affirmed on June 29, 2023 (316 Ga. 718), holding that, under the jury instructions given, the verdict apportioning no fault to the shooter was not inconsistent. Amount recorded is the adjusted (net of comparative fault) award; no attorney's fees are stated.
outcome.finalNote: Affirmed by the Court of Appeals (2021) and the Supreme Court of Georgia (2023).
